entries.title: New painted icons
items: Every spell has a new hand-painted icon in a thin frame in your class's colour, so a mage's spells and a warrior's look different at a glance. Fireball is a fireball now, not a snowflake.
Passive abilities look like soft badges with no frame, so you can tell them apart from things you press.
Items in your bag, the shops and the loot windows have their own painted pictures in square frames coloured by rarity: grey, blue, yellow, orange. Things you cannot use yet carry a small red badge.
Icons sit centred in their slots on phones too.

entries.title: Ashfield, the Catacombs, and a world of regions
items: The world now has regions, each with its own level range. Walk to the end of the Lark Road east of the Vale and you can travel to Ashfield. A loading screen shows where you are going.

Ashfield (levels 3-8): a lantern-lit hamlet at a crossroads with six new quests, and a huge walled cemetery in the fog. Every gravestone has a name. Some graves are open: dig in for coins and rings, but sometimes a skeleton, or someone with a name, climbs out.

The Catacombs (levels 6-8), under the Mausoleum Hill: ossuaries, enormous halls of columns where goblins have dug in, a troll, and the Deep King on his throne. Monsters only notice you when they can see you, so walls and pillars hide you.
Brightwater Vale is now levels 1-5 from end to end, and you level up faster early on. The whole Vale story takes you to about level 6, ready for Ashfield.
XP works like other online RPGs: monsters 5 or more levels below you give nothing, ones above you give up to 25% more. In a group everyone gets the full XP, so a high-level friend can help you along.
Shrines you find work as waypoints between regions: travel from any shrine to any shrine your world has found.
The map (M) opens on Places: every region, town and waypoint, sorted by level, with how to get there if you have not found it yet. The region map is the second tab.
Quest waypoints: the quest you mark gets a gold diamond on the minimap and the map, and a marker in the world with its distance. If it is in another region, it points to the road that leads there.
The quest tracker shows up to three quests with their region, step and distance, on phones too. Tap one to mark it.
Goblins, boars, wolves, bears and other monsters that looked tiny are now the size they should be.
On phones the Use button is now a small round button above Dodge with one word (Talk, Open, Travel…), only when something is in reach.
The arena panel is see-through, and the waves show as symbols: a tick for waves beaten, a skull for the brute wave and a crown for the boss.
The place name under the minimap fits on one line on phones.
Menus that cover nearly the whole screen now open full screen, and spell pictures in lists are round and centred again.

entries.title: Gear that is worth finding
items: Better gear is much better now. A weapon or armour piece from tougher monsters has a stronger base: about 12% more damage (10% more armour) for every item level.
Blue, yellow and orange items roll extra power on top: Magic +20-40%, Rare +45-75%, Legendary +80-120% damage or armour, shown as its own line on the card ("+38% enhanced damage").
A rare is never weaker than the same plain item any more.
Names show the step up: Steel, Tempered and Masterwork weapons and mail; Tanned and Hardened leather; Woven and Silk cloth.
Your starting weapon no longer grows with your level, so finding and buying upgrades is how you get stronger. Blues and yellows also drop a little more often.
Plate armour no longer drops before item level 4 (the mail version of the piece drops instead), so early finds are gear you can wear.
The Take button in a loot window works again.
The arena shows only your own reward chests by the board, and each one opens.
The points-left bubble in the Classes window counts down the moment you learn something.
Spears look like spears.
The flickering walls by the arena's Heroes' Gate are fixed.

entries.title: Weather, a fairer start, dodging that works, and a camera you can tune
items: Weather: clear skies, clouds, rain, fog and thunderstorms with lightning that lights the ground and thunder that rolls in late. Everyone in a world sees the same sky; the Thornmere Wilds are wetter and stormier than the Vale. Puddles grow in the rain.
Trees, grass and rain sway together in one wind, from a calm breeze to a storm that bends the forest.

A Look setting in Settings → Graphics: Classic (as before), Vivid, Cinematic, Moody or your own. Light shafts, softer longer shadows, shining water with foam at the shore, a richer sky and a wet look in the rain. Each effect says what it costs on a phone.
Dodging works: a monster's big blow now shows a red mark and lands exactly where the mark is, so a roll out of it is safe. Ordinary blows are quick, softer and have no mark.
A gentler start: monsters of levels 1-4 have less health and hit a little softer, and a new hero starts with more health.
"Miss" only shows when a blow was aimed at someone, not every time you swing at the air.

Weapon swings leave a trail along the blade: a bright steel streak with sparks for swords and daggers, a heavier trail with dust for axes and maces. Arrows fly as real arrows, and a monster's big blow cracks the ground.
Towns look better: painted walls, timber, stone and roofs, window boxes, shutters, shop signs, balconies, porches, ivy, lanterns and chimneys.
The stone bridges stand higher over the water and the Troll Bridge reaches further onto the banks.
Tune camera in the ☰ menu: move the camera's height, side offset, how far ahead it looks and more while you play, and send your numbers to us.
Send a lag report in the ☰ menu: if the game stutters, it shows what the last two minutes looked like and sends the details so we can fix it.

entries.title: The Arena: waves, reward chests and champions
items: New arena on the world list: a great arena of its own, with a court of shops outside its gates. Share its code like a world; up to 10 heroes.

Pick a bracket on the board by your level (1-2 up to 9-10) and fight five waves through four gates: a brute in wave 3, a boss in wave 5, a short breather between them. A level-1 hero can start; brackets above you are marked hard, never locked.
Win and a reward chest waits for each of you in the court: gear of the bracket's level and gold. The first win of a bracket adds a piece and a magic one for sure.
Ten champions, rank 10 to the Grand Champion, fight like heroes: their own abilities, rolls and a red mark before every big blow. Beat one for their unique item and a title shown with your name.
Your hero is the same everywhere: levels, gold, gear and titles from the arena come with you into your worlds.

entries.title: Combat rebuilt: big spells, knockdowns, new class trees
items: Every class tree is new: no more paths, several choices at every level, and every icon is one pick. Stronger ranks of a spell (Cleave II, Cleave III) are their own icons further down the tree.

Each weapon and armour kind is its own training (Sword, Axe, Mace, Two-Handed, Wand, Plate…), and a weapon Mastery gives +25% damage with that weapon. Passives and talents give big numbers now: +25%, not +2%.

Abilities are areas: novas round you, cones, lines, circles on the ground, leaps and charges. Big ones throw enemies through the air and knock them flat. Warrior Ground Slam flattens everything round you.
The Mage starts with Fireball: a huge spinning ball trailing embers that explodes and throws everything near it.
Every spell and attack looks about three times bigger, at its real size, with a swing or cast the moment you press the key — and phones now get the full effects.
Wands never fire a plain single bolt any more: every wand fans, chains, bursts, sprays a cone, rings or leaves burning ground.
Enemies wind up before every blow (a red mark on the ground) so you can roll out of the way. The dodge roll is longer and snappier.
Monsters come alone or in twos now, not packs of five, and fights are rebalanced so one-on-one is a fair fight.
Trees are drawn properly on every setting, and their lowest branches sit above the camera so they no longer hide enemies.
The phone Use button is gone (the prompt on screen does the same), and menus no longer open a tooltip on their own.
Your character keeps their levels: old class points come back to spend on the new trees.

entries.title: Smoother towns
items: Walking into a busy town no longer freezes the game for a moment: townsfolk are dressed and given their faces far faster (most noticeable on phones and older computers).

entries.title: Room to breathe
items: Towns have wider streets, houses stand back a little from the road, every house outside the very middle has its own fenced yard, and the edge of town spreads out. No more houses standing in the corn.
Peaceful animals (deer, sheep, cows, horses, hens, raccoons) show no name or health bar until you target or hurt them.
Shields block by themselves: a chance to stop part of a blow from the front, shown on your sheet and on the shield. The block button is gone.
No more run button: everyone walks about 15% faster. On phones the Attack, Dodge and Use buttons are bigger.
Levelling up: tap a skill to read everything about it first; a separate button spends the point.
Bridges are built properly now, and the invisible wall at the end of the Lark Bridge is gone.
Fixed: trees and rocks that blocked you but were not drawn on lower graphics settings; dark patches on the sides of timber houses.
The "Rate this game" option is gone.

entries.title: A wilder world
items: Wildlife everywhere: deer herds in the meadows and woods, wild horses on the downs, raccoons on the riverbanks, bats round the haunted places, more wolves and boars, and cows, a bull, sheep and hens round Larkford.

Animals and monsters no longer stand still: they wander and graze round their home until something catches their eye. Deer, horses, sheep, hens and raccoons run from you; cows and the bull only fight if you hit them.
Rats in the mill and the corn fields, for a first easy fight.
Big camps are split into small groups you can take one at a time; the Goblin Warren now has two outer pickets, the shamans' fire and the warchief at the back, and they notice you from closer.
Two new hamlets on the Lark Road, Crossbrook in the vale and Fernstead in the Wilds, and travellers walking the roads between them.
Looting: opening one body opens every body of yours close by in the same window; Take all and Take gold sweep them all, and the window closes itself when everything is taken.
Rings and amulets never ask for a level.
Animals that will not start a fight (deer, horses, sheep, hens, raccoons, cows, the bull) have a yellow name and bar; enemies stay red.

entries.title: Living towns
items: Larkford is a real town now: tall timber, stone and plaster houses packed shoulder to shoulder along a high street, a ring lane, West Street up the hill and narrow alleys, every house its own colours.
The town follows its hill: houses stand on stone footings with steps up to their doors, and the square, the shrine yard and the tower terrace are level terraces with walls round them.
Back yards behind the houses, with fences, hedges and low walls, woodpiles, crates and vegetable beds. Big trees stand in the open ground between the houses.
A market square with stalls, a fountain and benches; lamps along every street; shops with awnings, banners and goods at the door; smoke from the chimneys.
Villagers walk the streets, stop at the stalls and the fountain and go in and out of doors. They are just villagers: you cannot talk to them.

Townspeople work at their own spot: the shopkeeper behind the stall, the blacksmith at the anvil, the innkeeper at the inn door, trainers drilling at the training yard. They turn to you when you come close.
People are called by their job (the Blacksmith, the Shopkeeper, the Innkeeper…); only the people of the main story keep their names.
Thornwatch has log cabins along its lanes, yards and trees.
Shops: tapping or clicking an item shows its details first; a separate Buy or Sell button does the trade.

Enchanting moved to your own Trade skills window (K, or the ☰ menu): break items to learn enchantments and put them on your gear anywhere outside a fight. Shrines no longer do it. Repairs also show the item first, then a Repair button.
Phones: your first ability button works again (an invisible camera-drag area was covering it).
Picking an item in your bag shows everything about it: what it does with its numbers, each requirement next to what you have, and how it compares with what you wear.

Gear now asks mostly for attributes and training instead of level: leather wants Dexterity or Wisdom, mail Strength or Constitution, plate Strength, swords Strength or Dexterity, staves and tomes Intelligence or Wisdom, a little more on better pieces. Only rare and better items still ask for a level, and well below their own.

entries.title: Air, light and life
items: A warm late-afternoon sun with long shadows, and the sky itself now lights the world, so armour and water pick up its blue.
Soft cloud shadows drift across the land, a thin mist gathers in the river bottoms, and far hills rise beyond the haze.
Woods have an understory: bushes at the feet of trees, and saplings and shrubs where a wood thins into meadow. Leaves glow when the sun shines through them.
Leaf litter darkens the ground under trees, and the grass has yellower and deeper-green patches.
Smoke rises from chimneys, leaves drift down from the trees near you, dust floats in the light, birds wheel overhead and butterflies flit over the meadows.
You can hear where you are: birdsong in the woods, bustle in town, frogs by the marsh, wind in the open.
Rivers ripple and catch the sky. Buildings and props sit into the ground instead of floating on it.
On computers, a light colour grade and a soft glow on the brightest things; High graphics adds soft shade where things meet the ground and longer shadows.
Graphics quality is picked for your device on your first visit, and steps down once by itself if the game runs slowly (your own choice in Settings always stays).

entries.title: Tap the world, fuller forests
items: On a phone, tap a person to talk, tap a fallen enemy's remains to search them, tap a chest or a shrine to open it. If it's too far, your hero walks over first.
With a free mouse on a computer, clicking a person, remains, a chest or a shrine does the same.
"Wake at the shrine" works on phones when you fall (the button was hidden under the screen's look area).
The "Talk to…" / "Search…" prompt is a button you can tap. On phones it sits above your action buttons, out of the way of what's in front of you.
Making a hero is now four pages: your look, then your class with its whole skill tree to explore, then your background, then your attributes with the health, mana and damage you'll start with.
Trees have full, round crowns of big leaves, and pines are soft needle tiers, near and far and on every graphics setting. They used to be a few huge flat leaves on low graphics.
Phones: the Attack button looks like one, empty spell slots no longer fill two rows, and button hints say Tap instead of keyboard keys.

entries.title: A world worth walking
items: The trees are giants now: oaks, birches and pines tower 20 to 30 metres over you, and the old ancient oaks and great spruces deep in the woods reach past 40.
Every camp, shrine, ruin, grave, wall and chest is a real piece of the world: tents and banners, glowing shrines, carved standing stones, iron-banded chests that look as rich as what's inside.
Towns have cobbled squares and streets, worn dirt roads lead between them, and the fields are planted in strips of wheat, cabbage, pumpkins and more behind split-rail fences.
The ground has grass that sways, the sky has a sun and drifting clouds, and the light is warmer.
You can swim: wade into a river and swim across, then climb out on the far bank. (Your horse won't follow you in.)
Dodging is a quick dash the way you're moving, or toward your crosshair when you stand still, with no jump back.
The townsfolk are all properly dressed people now, and the camera stays in front of walls and trees.
Windows keep their place: the class tree, your bag and your talents no longer jump back to the start while open.

entries.title: Wands with a will of their own
items: Every wand now has its own attack: a straight bolt, a bursting one, a fan of three, a bolt that jumps between enemies, one that turns to follow, a slow heavy one, a cone, a beam, a ring around you, a lobbed blast, a forking bolt, a shielding bolt, or one that leaves the ground burning.
Tomes attack too, slower and harder: a Rune drawn on the ground, a Column of light, a Gale, or a Brand that scorches where it lands.
Staves cast their element's spell (a cone, a ring, a wave, a lobbed flask, a chain, or burning ground), or a Lance, or an Aegis Ring that shields you and your friends.
Sceptres swing in melee and hit with their element instead of steel.
An orb or focus in your off hand adds to a wand, tome or sceptre: an echo of every fourth attack, a burst round the enemy you hit, a shield, or mana back. A tome in the off hand echoes too.
Each item's card says exactly what its attack does, with your own damage numbers. Look out for the Wand of the Ninth Star and other named pieces from bosses, and the tome from The Lost Tome.

entries.title: The first oath
items: Brightwater Vale and Thornmere Wilds are open: two regions, two towns, camps, shrines and 23 quests.
Make a hero, then pick a class every time you level up — mix as many as you like.
Play alone or with up to 10 friends in a world that remembers what you did together.
Every corpse and chest has its own loot for each player, and gold has to be picked up.
Aim attacks and spells from over the shoulder; ground spells show where they will land.
Works with mouse and keyboard, a controller, or a phone.
